statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Insufficient facts to determine whether 31 U.S.C. § 5324 applies (i.e., whether there was structuring or other conduct done for the purpose of evading a Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirement).
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits (among other things) structuring or attempting to structure transactions, or causing/attempting to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file required reports, when done “for the purpose of evading” BSA reporting requirements (e.g., CTR reporting on currency transactions). Here, the fact pattern shows multiple large transactions (including many labeled “cash”) by a grocery/convenience business, but it does not state (1) whether any of the cash transactions were deposits/withdrawals with a domestic financial institution that would trigger a CTR, (2) whether any transactions were broken into amounts below a reporting threshold (e.g., multiple same-day cash transactions aggregating over $10,000), (3) whether any report was required and not filed, or (4) any evidence of intent/purpose to evade reporting. Because § 5324’s key element is purpose/intent to evade and the record lacks facts showing structuring behavior around a reporting threshold or intent to evade, § 5324 prohibits structuring cannot be conclusively applied or ruled out on these facts.
